spec.title: Four counters, one control question
spec.intro:
One control question — "list every user and whether MFA is on" — takes four wire shapes. You are
handed the four machine-readable contracts (OpenAPI, WSDL, GraphQL SDL, .proto) and four real
clean/broken capture pairs over the SAME eight users, and asked to LOCATE the MFA truth-field in
each contract, decode the gRPC frame down to the literal bytes, recompute a SOAP credential
digest, and click the single field where each broken capture breaks its control.

Every value you reveal is the real parser/decoder/transform over the real artifact — the same
bytes protobuf.dev verifies (a=150 → 08 96 01) and the spec grammars define. Nothing is invented;
the decoder is the answer key. Start on the REST OpenAPI contract panel.

tasks.instruction:
On the "Contract · REST OpenAPI 3.1" panel, expand to and select the node that declares the
MFA truth-field — `components.schemas.User.properties.mfa_enabled`. Read its declared JSON type.

hints.nudge: The contract is the FIRST place a control's truth lives — find the field that names mfa, before any live call.

hints.reveal: Select components.schemas.User.properties.mfa_enabled; its declared type is boolean

tasks.explain:
Before you ever hit a live endpoint, the OpenAPI doc told you where the MFA truth-field is and
that it is a boolean. The static contract is collectible evidence — the auditor's first artifact.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "Contract · SOAP WSDL + WS-SecurityPolicy" and select the `sp:SignedParts` policy
node — the assertion proving the SOAP message Body MUST be signed (the integrity control SOAP invites).

hints.nudge: SOAP's control lives in the WS-SecurityPolicy, not an HTTP header — find the signing requirement.

hints.concept: §4.1 — WSDL portType carries intent; sp:SignedParts requires the Body signed

hints.reveal: Select the sp:SignedParts node — it requires the SOAP Body be signed (message integrity)

tasks.explain:
Unlike REST/GraphQL/gRPC (header bearer), SOAP protects the message itself. sp:SignedParts is
the WS-SecurityPolicy assertion that makes message-level integrity a contractual requirement.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "Contract · GraphQL SDL" and select the `User.mfaEnabled` field node. Read its
GraphQL type. Then note: the SAME truth-field, a third name, a third shape.

hints.nudge: In SDL the truth-field is a typed field inside `type User { … }`.

hints.concept: §4.1 — GraphQL SDL: type User { email mfaEnabled: Boolean! }

hints.reveal: Select User.mfaEnabled; its type is Boolean! (non-null boolean)

tasks.explain:
REST calls it mfa_enabled (snake_case JSON), GraphQL calls it mfaEnabled (camelCase Boolean!).
One control-truth, four contract names — you LOCATE it by reading the contract, not from memory.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "Contract · gRPC .proto" and select the `User.mfa_enabled` field. Read its field
TAG — the load-bearing number `= 2` the wire encoder will turn into a byte.

hints.nudge: In a .proto, every field has a `= N` tag — that N, not the name, is what the wire carries.

hints.concept: §4.5 — bool mfa_enabled = 2; the `= 2` is the field tag the protobuf wire encodes

hints.reveal: Select bool mfa_enabled = 2; its field tag is 2 (the number the wire encodes)

tasks.explain:
The .proto field tag `= 2` is the bridge to the wire: protobuf encodes tag = (2 << 3) | 0 = 0x10
for this VARINT bool field. You just read the number you will see as a byte two tasks from now.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "GraphQL · clean: precise" and select the `max selection depth` node, then the
`introspection present` node. Confirm the precise query is shallow and reveals no schema.

hints.nudge: A precise GraphQL query names only the fields it needs — its depth is small and it asks for no schema.

hints.concept: §4.4 — precision is the feature: { users { email mfaEnabled } } is depth 2, no introspection

hints.reveal: Select max-selection-depth on the clean GraphQL query; it reads 2

tasks.explain:
`{ users { email mfaEnabled } }` is depth 2 with introspection off — the precision GraphQL is
praised for. The next panels show that same precision turned into a weapon.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "gRPC · clean" and select the `:path` pseudo-header. gRPC carries intent in the
`:path`, not an HTTP verb. Confirm it routes to the ListUsers RPC.

hints.nudge: gRPC has no GET/POST verb intent — the operation is the HTTP/2 :path pseudo-header.

hints.concept: §4.2 — gRPC intent is the :path /package.Service/Method, not a verb

tasks.explain:
Where REST's intent is the verb and SOAP's is the body operation, gRPC's intent is the :path.
Same question, fourth shape — and the :path is where an auditor reads which RPC was called.

tasks.instruction:
Still on "gRPC · clean", drill the message body to the second user's `mfa_enabled` field
(node `body.grpc.message.f1_2.f2_2`). Calibrate on protobuf.dev's a=150 → 08 96 01, then
confirm this field decodes to `false` via tag 0x10 (field 2, VARINT) and value 0x00.

hints.nudge: tag = (field_number << 3) | wire_type. Field 2 as a VARINT (wire type 0) is (2<<3)|0 = 0x10; a false bool is 0x00.

hints.concept: §4.5 — protobuf: 0x10 is field 2 VARINT, 0x00 is false. mfa_enabled=false = 0x10 0x00

hints.reveal: Select body.grpc.message.f1_2.f2_2 — it decodes to false (tag 0x10, value 0x00)

tasks.explain:
You just read a boolean off raw binary the same way you read JSON. `0x10 0x00` is `mfa_enabled =
false` — the second seeded user lacks MFA, and the decoder proved it, byte by byte. The opaque
gRPC frame is now as readable as any other paradigm.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "SOAP · clean". Select the `recomputed PasswordDigest` node — the transform's live
output Base64(SHA-1(Nonce+Created+password)) — and confirm it reproduces the envelope's stated
digest. The credential lives INSIDE the SOAP message, not in a header.

hints.nudge: A WS-Security PasswordDigest is recomputed, not trusted — feed Nonce, Created, and the password through the transform.

hints.concept: §4.3 — PasswordDigest = Base64(SHA-1(nonce + created + password)); the transform is the oracle

hints.reveal: Select the recomputed-digest node; it reproduces the envelope's AtYMdWClJo7PIuTpqmhmEEoEZyc=

tasks.explain:
The recomputed digest matches the clean envelope — proof the credential is intact. On the broken
SOAP twin, a stale Created makes this recompute disagree with the envelope, which is the replay
finding. You verify SOAP auth by recomputing, never by trusting the stamp.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "REST · broken". This response over-returns fields the contract never declared.
Select the `salary` property node — the single field that breaks the BOPLA control (API3).

hints.nudge: Diff the broken response against the clean sparse one — it carries properties the OpenAPI schema never declared.

hints.concept: §4.6 — REST fails by FIELD: returning salary/ssn the caller can't see is API3 (BOPLA)

hints.reveal: Select data[0].attributes.salary on the broken REST panel — it reads 185000, a field the contract never declared

tasks.explain:
The broken REST response leaks salary and ssn — Broken Object Property Level Authorization,
OWASP API3:2023. The contract declared only email and mfa_enabled; the runtime returned more.
The finding is the extra property, and the contract is the evidence it shouldn't be there.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "GraphQL · broken". Select the `max selection depth` node (a 12-deep circular query)
and confirm the depth. This is the depth-DoS the limiter must reject (API4). The real limiter
run is wired to this panel.

hints.nudge: The broken query nests a self-referencing field far past the cap — read its depth, then watch the real limiter reject it.

hints.concept: §4.4 — depth/cost DoS is API4; a 12-deep circular query trips the real depth limiter

hints.reveal: Select max-selection-depth (12) on the broken GraphQL panel; the limiter rejects it (exit 1, depth error)

tasks.explain:
Depth 12 past a cap of 6 is unrestricted resource consumption — OWASP API4:2023. The limiter
didn't say "try again"; it returned the real graphql-depth-limit error (exit 1). Proving the
depth and cost limiters are ON is the GraphQL control, not "GraphQL is unsafe."

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "gRPC · broken". Select the `:path` pseudo-header — it routes to the server-reflection
endpoint advertised in prod (API9). Confirm the reflection :path.

hints.nudge: gRPC fails by discoverability — a :path to the reflection service in prod leaks the whole API surface.

hints.concept: §4.6 — gRPC server reflection in prod is API9 (improper inventory); alg:none JWT is API2

hints.reveal: Select the :path on the broken gRPC panel — it routes to /grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection/ServerReflectionInfo

tasks.explain:
Server reflection in production lets anyone enumerate every RPC — Improper Inventory Management,
OWASP API9:2023. Paired with the alg:none JWT in the same capture's authorization header (API2),
this twin fails by discoverability AND auth. Reflection must be OFF in prod.

tasks.instruction:
Switch to "SOAP · broken". Select the `recomputed PasswordDigest` node and confirm it NO LONGER
matches the clean digest — the stale Created made the transform disagree with the envelope (replay, API2).

hints.nudge: The broken envelope's wsu:Created is stale — recompute the digest over the stale values and it won't match the envelope's stated digest.

hints.concept: §4.3 — a stale Created + a digest that no longer recomputes is a replay (API2)

hints.reveal: Select wsu:Created (stale) on the broken SOAP panel; the recomputed digest is now xsV9u/k/s5u5fCiDHO0Mx6IP92w=, not the envelope's value

tasks.explain:
The stale Created (2001) makes the recomputed digest diverge from the envelope's stated digest —
a replayed message, OWASP API2:2023 Broken Authentication. The disagreement is computed by the
transform over the real bytes, not asserted. Recompute, don't trust.

tasks.instruction:
In 5–7 sentences, for a non-technical colleague: explain why ONE control question ("does every
user have MFA?") takes four wire shapes, where each paradigm's contract lets you LOCATE the
truth-field, and the single control surface each invites (REST→field/API3, GraphQL→shape+
discoverability/API4+API9, SOAP→time+integrity/API2, gRPC→discoverability+auth/API9+API2). Use
the §3 four-counters model, not jargon.

hints.nudge: The §3 model: four counters, one question — each takes your request and hands back the answer differently.

hints.concept: §3 — The Mental Model + §4.6 the OWASP map

source.raw:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<wsdl:definitions name="UserService"
    targetNamespace="http://acme.example/users"
    xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/"
    xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/"
    xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"
    xmlns:wsp="http://www.w3.org/ns/ws-policy"
    xmlns:sp="http://docs.oasis-open.org/ws-sx/ws-securitypolicy/200702"
    xmlns:tns="http://acme.example/users">
  <wsdl:types>
    <xsd:schema targetNamespace="http://acme.example/users">
      <xsd:complexType name="User">
        <xsd:sequence>
          <xsd:element name="email" type="xsd:string"/>
          <xsd:element name="mfaEnabled" type="xsd:boolean"/>
          <xsd:element name="role" type="xsd:string"/>
        </xsd:sequence>
      </xsd:complexType>
    </xsd:schema>
  </wsdl:types>
  <wsdl:message name="ListUsersRequest"/>
  <wsdl:message name="ListUsersResponse">
    <wsdl:part name="users" type="tns:User"/>
  </wsdl:message>
  <wsdl:portType name="UserPortType">
    <wsdl:operation name="ListUsers">
      <wsdl:input message="tns:ListUsersRequest"/>
      <wsdl:output message="tns:ListUsersResponse"/>
    </wsdl:operation>
  </wsdl:portType>
  <wsdl:binding name="UserBinding" type="tns:UserPortType">
    <wsp:Policy>
      <sp:SignedParts>
        <sp:Body/>
      </sp:SignedParts>
      <sp:SupportingTokens>
        <wsp:Policy><sp:UsernameToken/></wsp:Policy>
      </sp:SupportingTokens>
    </wsp:Policy>
    <soap:binding style="document" transport="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/http"/>
    <wsdl:operation name="ListUsers">
      <soap:operation soapAction="http://acme.example/users/ListUsers"/>
    </wsdl:operation>
  </wsdl:binding>
</wsdl:definitions>

source.query: query { users { manager { manager { manager { manager { manager { manager { manager { manager { manager { manager { id } } } } } } } } } } __schema { types { name } } }

panels.label: SOAP · clean: fresh Created + matching digest
SOAP · broken: stale Created → digest mismatch (API2)
gRPC · clean: no reflection, signed JWT
gRPC · broken: reflection enabled + alg:none JWT (API9+API2)
